Algorithm Finite sequence of well-defined steps to solve a problem. Characteristics: input (zero or more), output (at least one), definiteness (each step clear), finiteness (ends after finite steps), effectiveness (each step basic and doable). Flow of Control Sequence — statements executed one after another. Selection (decision) — choose a path based on a condition: if, if-else, switch. Iteration (repetition/loop) — repeat steps: for, while, do-while. Any algorithm can be built from these three constructs (structured programming).

Verifying & Comparing Algorithms Verification — dry run (trace by hand with sample inputs) to check the algorithm gives correct output. Comparison — by time complexity (number of steps) and space complexity (memory). E.g. to check prime, testing divisors up to √n is faster than up to n−1.
